study_type_evidence.quote: The pharmacokinetics of SNIO–CBP was assessed in healthy male mice using dynamic T1-weighted MRI
The final solution was 200 µL in volume, contained 6 mM SNIO–CBP on a per-Fe basis and 10% FBS. The mixture was incubated at 37 °C
Affinity between SNIO–CBP and human type I collagen was investigated in vitro, and a collagen-binding dissociation constant Kd = 18.4 µM was measured

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: healthy/normal male mice (n = 3) for the pharmacokinetic imaging; strain and age not stated for this group
in_vivo_species.quote: The pharmacokinetics of SNIO–CBP was assessed in healthy male mice using dynamic T1-weighted MRI

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male C57BL/6, 6 weeks old at study start, Charles River Laboratories (CCl4 liver fibrosis model, dosed 12 wk)
in_vivo_species.quote: Male C57BL/6 mice (6-wk-old, Charles River Laboratories) were treated with an oral gavage of carbon tetrachloride for 12 wk

in_vivo_species.strain_sex_age: male C57BL/6, 6 weeks old, Charles River Labs (CDAHFD NASH model, fed 14 wk)
in_vivo_species.quote: To induce NASH, 6-wk-old, male C57BL/6 mice (Charles River Labs) were fed CDAHFD (n = 6) ... for 14 wk.

ex_vivo_detail: Nonspecific-binding assessment of SNIO–CBP in bovine serum: SNIO–CBP (6 mM Fe) incubated with 10% or 20% fetal bovine serum at 37 C for 5 min and analysed by size-exclusion chromatography. This is a serum-binding, not a serum-stability, assay. Liver tissue was also collected post-mortem for Sirius Red / H&E / Prussian Blue staining and hydroxyproline HPLC quantification.
in_vitro_detail: Cell-free assays only: human type I collagen binding affinity in 96-well gelled collagen films with ICP-MS readout (Kd = 18.4 µM); longitudinal relaxivity (r1) measurements at 1.41 T and 4.7 T in PBS; SAXS and gel-filtration sizing. No cell culture was used.

agents.name: SNIO–CBP (single-nanometer iron oxide nanoparticle conjugated to type I collagen-binding peptide)
agents.sequence_source: The body states only that the vector is a 'type I collagen-binding peptide (CBP)' obtained from AmbioPharm; no amino-acid sequence is printed anywhere in the body or figure captions.
agents.chemical_identifier: SNIO–CBP; iron oxide core 1.5 nm by SAXS, hydrodynamic diameter 4.6 nm by GFC, SNIO/CBP ratio 1/1.1, Fe/CBP 54/1, zeta potential −4.67 mV; CBP–azide LC-MS m/z [M+2]/2 = 1280.3, [M+3]/3 = 254.3
agents.group_n: n = 3 (pharmacokinetics in normal mice); n = 6 CCl4 and n = 4 olive-oil control; n = 6 CDAHFD and matched standard-chow controls
agents.group_n_quote: Clearance profile of SNIO–CBP in normal mice (n = 3).
agents.dose: 2 nmol/g body weight on a CBP basis
agents.route: intravenous (tail vein bolus while animal in scanner)
agents.dose_route_quote: Following intravenous administration (2 nmol SNIO–CBP/gram animal; all animal doses are reported on CBP basis), immediate blood pool enhancement was observed
agents.half_life_matrix: mouse blood pool (heart), measured as MRI contrast-to-noise ratio in vivo
agents.pk_quote: immediate blood pool enhancement was observed from whole-body MRI with a blood elimination half-life of 5.7 ± 1.9 min that was estimated from a monoexponential decay

agents.name: CM-101
agents.sequence_source: Described only as a gadolinium-based collagen-binding contrast agent sharing the same CBP as SNIO–CBP; no sequence printed.
agents.chemical_identifier: CM-101, gadolinium-based collagen-binding contrast agent, Gd/CBP ratio 3/1
agents.group_n: n = 6 (CCl4 group) and n = 4 (olive-oil control group)
agents.group_n_quote: Group 2, CCl4 for 12 wk (n = 6) and imaged with CM-101 (5 nmol/g CBP).
agents.dose: 5 nmol/g body weight on a CBP basis
agents.dose_route_quote: Doses of 2 nmol/g SNIO–CBP and 5 nmol/g CM-101 were used, and liver-to-muscle CNR was quantified
agents.half_life: not reported numerically; stated only as similar to SNIO–CBP
agents.pk_quote: This half-life was similar to the pharmacokinetics of the gadolinium-based CM-101.

agents.name: Unfunctionalized SNIO (single-nanometer iron oxide without peptide)
agents.chemical_identifier: SNIO with zwitterionic dopamine sulfonate coating
agents.group_n: not applicable (relaxivity measurement only, not administered)

agents.dose_route_quote: The r1 of SNIO–CBP was measured to be 4.5 s−1 (mM Fe)−1 at 1.4 T and 37 °C, 50% higher than unfunctionalized SNIO (3.0 s−1 mM−1)

concentration_time_figure.locator: Fig. 2A and Fig. 2B (also Fig. 3C and Fig. 4B for liver signal vs time)
concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Clearance profile of SNIO–CBP quantified through CNR in the blood pool, liver, and kidneys. CNR data were fitted into exponential decays.
concentration_time_figure.note: Fig. 2B plots MRI contrast-to-noise ratio (a surrogate for agent concentration, not an absolute concentration) versus time in blood pool, liver and kidney up to 32 min after a single i.v. dose; the 5.7 min blood half-life was derived from the monoexponential fit of this blood-pool curve.

bioanalytical_method: Dynamic T1-weighted MRI (3D FLASH, 4.7 T small-bore animal scanner) with contrast-to-noise-ratio quantification in Horos; 56Fe ICP-MS (45Sc internal standard) used for iron quantification of formulations and in the in vitro collagen-binding assay; enzymatic fluorometric L-amino acid assay for CBP content
bioanalytical_quote: The pharmacokinetics of SNIO–CBP was assessed in healthy male mice using dynamic T1-weighted MRI ... quantified by measuring changes in the tissue-to-muscle contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR)
bioanalytical_section: RESULTS / METHODS (MR Imaging; MRI Data Analysis)
notes: The only PK parameter in the body is the blood elimination half-life of SNIO–CBP (5.7 ± 1.9 min, n = 3 normal male mice, 2 nmol/g CBP i.v.), derived from a monoexponential fit of MRI blood-pool CNR rather than from measured plasma concentrations; no Cmax, Tmax, AUC, clearance or volume of distribution is reported, and no plasma assay of the agent was performed. The CBP amino-acid sequence is never printed in the body (only the PeplifeDB metadata header lists one, which per protocol cannot be used). CM-101 has no numeric PK in the body, only a qualitative statement of similarity. CCl4 and olive oil are listed as agents because they were administered, but they are disease-induction/vehicle-control treatments rather than test articles. The FBS incubation is recorded as ex vivo per protocol, though it assessed nonspecific protein binding rather than stability. Total of 35 mice studied.
